chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, from Al-Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'O Mufazzal! Listen to what I say to you, and know that it is the truth, and act upon it, and inform your brothers of the 'high standing' (Ilyat). I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is the high standing of my brothers?' He said: 'Those who are eager to fulfill the needs of their brothers.'

He said, then he said: 'And whoever fulfills a need for his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will fulfill for him on the Day of Resurrection a hundred thousand needs. From those, the first is Paradise, and from them is that He will admit his relatives, his acquaintances, and his brothers into Paradise, after they are not Nasibi (disbelievers in the Imams).'
And it was so that whenever Al-Mufazzal asked a brother from his brothers for a need, he would say to him, 'Do you not desire that you be among the high-standing brothers?'

key_terms.أَوَّلُهَا: The first of them (referring to the fulfilled needs)
key_terms.عِلْيَة: High social standing or elevated status
key_terms.نُصَّاب: Nasibi (one who is hostile to the Imams, specifically in Shia context)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for fulfilling the needs of a fellow believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates fulfilling the needs of believers to a defining characteristic of the 'high standing' (Ilyat) among the community, linking social solidarity directly to eschatological reward. The promise of Allah fulfilling a hundred thousand needs—including the intercession for one's kin to enter Paradise—underscores the transformative power of mutual aid in Shia spiritual ethics. This concept reinforces the communal bond (Ukhuwwah) as a means of purifying the believer's status and securing divine favor on the Day of Judgment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Bakkar Bin Kardam, from Al Mufazzal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Mufazzal!

Listen to what I<sup>asws</sup> am saying to you, and know that it is the truth, and do it (yourself) and inform your brothers of the high social standing’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what are my brothers of ‘high social standing’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Those who are interested in fulfilling the needs of their brethren’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then heasws said: ‘And the one who fulfils a need of his Momin brother, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Fulfil for him a hundred thousand needs of the Day of Judgement – from that the first one is the Paradise, and from that is that he would enter his relatives and his acquaintances, and his brethren into the Paradise, after (it is clarified) that they do not happen to be Hostile ones (Nasibis)’.

And it was so that whenever Al-Mufazzal (the narrator) asked for a need from a brother from his brethren, said to him, ‘Do you not desire that you happen to be from the brethren of high social standing?’
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Bakkar ibn Kardam from al-Mufaddal from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Imam said to me, ‘O Mufaddal, listen to what I say to you. Bear in mind that it is the truth. Do it and inform ‘Ilyat, of your brothers (in belief).’ I asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what is (Tlyah) of my brothers (in belief)?’ The Imam said, ‘All those interested in helping their brothers (in belief).’

The narrator has said that the Imam then said, ‘Whoever makes one wish of his brother (in belief) come true Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, on the Day of Judgment will make one thousand of his wishes come true of which one is his admission in paradise, as well as his relatives, those whom he knows and his brothers will be admitted into paradise, provided, they are not against belief in Walayah (Divine Authority) of ‘A ’immah.
Whenever al-Mufaddal would ask for help from any of his brothers (in belief) he would ask, ‘Do you not wish to be a ’Ilyah (brothers in belief) interested in helping believers?”’
